comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1-C3 regarding lineage tracing experiments. Both evaluations recognize the solid evidence from fate-mapping models (Tnfsf11aCre and Flt3Cre) and affirm the complementary approach as a major strength of the study.

Perfect agreement on claims C4-C6 regarding ΔFIRE model specificity. Both evaluations praise the selective depletion of EMP-derived macrophages as a major strength and accept the specificity demonstrated by flow cytometry and lineage tracing data.

Agreement on claims C7-C8 regarding DT-mediated depletion lethality. OpenEval explicitly supports the survival and physiological data, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this rationale by endorsing the ΔFIRE model without questioning the absence of DT depletion experiments.

Perfect agreement on claims C9-C15 regarding baseline scRNA-seq characterization. Both evaluations recognize the robust methodology and accept the specific cluster depletion patterns and correlation with YFP expression in ΔFIRE mice.

Perfect agreement on claims C16-C17 regarding altered immune cell gene expression at baseline. Both evaluations support the findings of changes in non-macrophage populations and altered immune cell crosstalk, though OpenEval notes the functional significance requires further investigation.

Strong agreement on claims C18-C21 regarding impaired cardiac functional recovery. Both evaluations accept the PET imaging data showing differential trajectories between control and ΔFIRE mice. Peer review R6 also addresses C22-C23 (infarct size), which OpenEval covers separately in R7.

Agreement on claims C22-C23 regarding unchanged infarct size in ΔFIRE mice. OpenEval emphasizes this distinguishes remodeling effects from infarct size effects. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'the absence of resident macrophages is not influencing infarct size,' grouping this with functional outcomes.

Perfect agreement on claims C24-C31 regarding spatial distribution of macrophage populations after injury. Both evaluations accept the lineage tracing and immunohistology data showing sustained resident macrophage depletion in remote zones and normal BM-derived macrophage recruitment to injury sites.

Perfect agreement on claims C32-C37 regarding transcriptional differences between resident and recruited macrophages. Both evaluations support the bulk RNA-seq findings showing distinct functional programs, with peer reviewers noting this aligns with current understanding in the field.

Strong agreement on claims C38-C43 regarding enhanced pro-inflammatory phenotype after injury. Both evaluations support the scRNA-seq findings of cluster-specific changes and inflammasome activation. Peer review R9 also addresses C44-C47 (ligand-receptor interactions), which OpenEval covers separately in R11.

Agreement on claims C44-C47 regarding reduced intercellular communication from resident macrophage clusters. OpenEval provides detailed support for ligand-receptor interaction analysis. Peer reviewers confirm altered immune cell crosstalk findings, grouping these with inflammatory phenotype changes.

Strong agreement on claims C48-C51 regarding effective macrophage depletion with PLX5622 treatment. Both evaluations accept the flow cytometry and histology data. Peer review R10 groups these with C52-C55 (functional outcomes), which OpenEval covers separately in R13.

Agreement on claims C52-C55 regarding worse outcomes with combined macrophage depletion (PLX5622). Both evaluations support the findings of reduced cardiac function and increased fibrosis when both resident and recruited macrophages are depleted.

Strong agreement on claims C56-C59 regarding differential effects of the two depletion models. Both evaluations accept the comparative analysis showing recruited macrophages are beneficial. Peer review R11 also addresses C60-C61 (main conclusions), which OpenEval covers separately in R15.

Perfect agreement on claims C60-C61 representing the main conclusions. Both evaluations strongly support the central finding that resident and recruited macrophages have distinct functions. All peer reviewers explicitly endorse these conclusions as important contributions to the field.

OpenEval evaluated claims C62-C82 regarding background literature citations and found them appropriately supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation explicitly addresses these background claims, as peer reviewers focused on experimental findings rather than citation accuracy.
